lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Chapter heading.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For the first hour, Uruk remained behind them as a black interruption in the western sky.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The city wall followed at their backs, visible whenever the land flattened and disappearing whenever the old irrigation ridges rose between them and the torches. From this distance, the watch fires looked pinned to the darkness. They did not seem to move, though Zeek knew guards were pacing above the bricks, looking outward for enemies and inward for citizens who had discovered unofficial uses for drainage channels.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The ground beyond the wall was not yet desert. Abandoned fields lay beneath the darkness, divided by dry canals and low embankments. Thorn scrub crowded the old channels. Rainwater gathered in the deeper ruts, turning dust into mud that clung to their sandals.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg walked behind Zeek, breathing heavily beneath his pack.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You said that half a league ago.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: No. I said we would not stop until sunrise.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun stepped over a collapsed section of canal wall and nearly lost her footing. BAH-lahg caught the back of her satchel before she went down.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You almost fell into a ditch.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I identified the ditch before entering it.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: An archaeologist uses the instruments available.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo moved ahead of them, barely visible except when she crossed a strip of open ground. She had removed the pale wrapping from her hair and replaced it with dark cloth. Mud had dulled the lower half of her robes. One hand remained close to her knife.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She stopped at the top of an embankment and raised two fingers.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The night carried small sounds farther than daylight did: water dripping from reeds, insects clicking beneath the thorn, BAH-lahg's breathing, Ninsun trying not to breathe loudly enough for BAH-lahg to comment on it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Beyond those sounds came the soft creak of leather.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg's hand moved toward his axe.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo crouched, peered down the far side of the embankment, and looked back at Zeek.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: You did not ask how I intended to cross the desert carrying four lamps, a hammer, two ropes, and Ninsun's private library.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun adjusted the satchel against her chest.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg climbed the embankment beside en-HEH-doo.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Below them stood the ruins of a small field shelter. Three mud-brick walls remained. The fourth had collapsed into the dry canal. A roof of bundled reeds sagged above one corner.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: One was gray, narrow-faced, and watching the group with immediate suspicion. The other was brown and already attempting to chew through the rope that secured it to a post.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You left animals outside the city wall.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I paid a farmer to leave them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo looked around the abandoned fields.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: He is reliable because he understands distance.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The gray donkey flattened its ears at him.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: You have that effect on thoughtful animals.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg held out one hand and spoke softly.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The donkey considered him, then allowed him to touch its muzzle.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I expected Uruk to become inconvenient.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: That is not the same thing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo entered the shelter and examined the shadows beneath the remaining roof. She checked behind the fallen bricks, beneath the reed matting, and inside a cracked storage jar.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: He was instructed not to wait.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: The ground beneath the roof is dry.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The animals had churned the dirt around the post. Their hoofprints overlapped in circles. Beyond those marks, the floor of the shelter remained smooth.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg ran his hand along the gray donkey's flank.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A bundle of barley stalks lay between the animals. Half had been eaten.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo looked toward the dark fields.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Your farmer came without touching the ground?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: He was always light on his feet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek moved to the brown donkey and untied the rope. The animal immediately tried to bite the bronze fitting on his satchel.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Do that again and you carry BAH-lahg.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The donkey looked at BAH-lahg, then stopped.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg inspected every strap, knot, blanket, and buckle before allowing anyone to load the animals. He found one split leather loop, replaced it with cord, then found fault with the cord and replaced that with a strip cut from his spare belt.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo leaned against the broken wall and watched the fields.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun stood near Zeek with BAYL-ID-din's warning folded inside her robe.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You did not tell us about the animals.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You also did not tell us about the seal until the Collector placed it on the floor.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I had not known about the seal.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek tightened a strap around a waterskin.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You have not told us everything it wrote.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I told you about the map.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You told us enough to make following you seem slightly less irrational.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: That is why archives are full of people arguing over marks made by accountants.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun stepped into his path when he reached for the next pack.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind her, BAH-lahg pretended to be occupied with a saddle blanket. His hands had gone still.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo continued watching the fields, though her head had turned enough to hear them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It moves whenever it dislikes the conversation.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: It knocked after he called you BAYL-ID-din's successor.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It also knocked inside a wall.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: That is not an argument against meaning.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It is an argument against expecting clarity.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: What else did your father write?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The darkness beneath her eyes had deepened since the archive. She had copied the map until her fingers cramped, then packed the copies as carefully as if they were royal decrees. Mud streaked the hem of her robe. A loose strand of hair had stuck to her cheek.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She had followed him through a wall, across the roofs, beneath the city, and into fields where animals appeared without footprints.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: He wrote that he was wrong about the depth,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal pressed once against Zeek's ribs.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Her eyes dropped to the satchel.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: What did it say after we left the city?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg resumed pulling at a strap that required no adjustment.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You should lie more carefully around objects that contradict you.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek put both hands on the brown donkey's pack frame.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: And something below the drainage channel answered with the same pattern.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg tied off the strap and avoided his eyes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun opened her satchel and began searching through it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You need all of them. That is the problem.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She pulled free a narrow clay copy wrapped in linen.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I have stopped asking what she carries.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun unwrapped the tablet and held it close to the faint starlight.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: This is from the lower archive. A funerary fragment from the Old Kings period.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I think the classification was convenient.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo left the shelter's edge and approached.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Not enough. The beginning is broken. The surviving portion describes a descent through seven gates.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg gave a quiet sound in his throat.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: My grandfather told stories about seven gates.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Most warnings become myths after enough people ignore them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun ran her thumb above the copied signs without touching them.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The traveler surrendered something at each threshold.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: At the first gate, a covering.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Possibly. At the second, ornament. At the third, rank. The fourth passage is damaged.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked toward the drainage channel hidden beyond the fields.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The surviving sign can mean name, declaration, or recognized identity.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek touched the pouch beneath his robe.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The bronze seal lay cold against his chest.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It tells the door what stands before it,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I examined it in a room where a man had climbed away with his hands pointing in the wrong direction. I was distracted.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek drew the pouch from beneath his robe and removed the bronze seal.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The lines remained dark where they had changed beneath his marked palm. Mud had dried around the rim, but the grooves were clean.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She turned it toward the east, where the first thin suggestion of dawn had begun to separate the sky from the land.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: My grandfather's version had no clothing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: First gate took a man's shadow. Second took the voice people knew him by. Third took the hand he trusted. After that, the story changed depending on how much beer my grandfather had.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The gray donkey shifted beside him.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Its hoof struck the ground four times.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg took hold of the animal's halter.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: It has mud in its shoe.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Then it has mud in whatever you call the part I need to blame.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo looked toward the fields again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg stroked the animal's neck until it settled.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: The man reaches the seventh gate.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: He has nothing left that the gate can take.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: No. It means the gate takes what is left.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Shapes emerged from the darkness: dead canals, thorn clusters, the low swells of abandoned fields. Farther east, the cultivated ground thinned into scrub. Beyond that waited the open desert.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun handed the seal back to Zeek.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The lower archive contains other fragments. Some say clothing and jewelry. Some say memory, title, ancestry. One version says the final gate requires the living traveler to surrender the last thing that separates the living from the dead.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Good. I was concerned it might become specific.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The translations may describe ritual disarmament,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: A ruler entering sacred space is stripped of rank and visible authority. Each gate removes a social identity.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Until the ruler is only a person,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: And then the last gate kills him.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg gave Zeek a flat look.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I am relieved the ancient priests may have been murdering kings instead of feeding doors.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: That is the lowest standard for relief I have heard.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo rested one hand on the hilt of her knife.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: What if it is not ritual?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Her gaze shifted to the seal in Zeek's hand.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Or for preventing something from leaving.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The wind moved across the fields.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It came from the west, carrying the smell of wet brick, smoke, dung fires, and river mud.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The city had emerged behind them with the dawn.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It rose in layers above the wall, rooftops pressed close together, smoke already unwinding from ovens and workshops. The temple platforms caught the first light. Their upper walls burned red while the lower districts remained blue with shadow.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: No narrow figure standing between torches.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Uruk looked ancient enough to have invented permanence and arrogant enough to tax anyone who copied it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun came to stand beside him.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The texts call the place beyond the gates a city.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: You crossed a wall, a roof, a drainage passage, and three miles of mud to correct us now?

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The term translated as city can also mean ordered enclosure, inhabited foundation, or place under rule.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek felt the bronze seal warming in his palm.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Collector's voice returned to him.

lines.speaker: The Collector
lines.text: The City is not a tomb.
lines.note: Memory echo of the Collector's voice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek had dismissed the rest as a threat shaped to fit an old fear.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: But the old texts had been written before the Collector. Before BAYL-ID-din. Before KOO-rash raised the hammer over the black floor.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The accounts do not describe people building the First City.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The gray donkey snorted behind them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A bird called from the reeds near the dry canal.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The ordinary sound made the silence afterward worse.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked at the ruined shelter.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: If this is a gate, where is the door?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun considered the fields, the hidden drainage passage, and Uruk beyond them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo's gaze went to the wall.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Ritual accounts often preserve function rather than architecture.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: That sentence was designed to excuse anything.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: It was designed to explain why old texts should not be read like building plans.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Checking whether the journal has decided to become useful.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: That thing has never been useful. It has been accurate. Those are not the same.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The cover was dry despite the mud and rain that had soaked the satchel. The scar along its surface caught the dawn like a thin line of oil.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun moved close enough to see.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg muttered something that sounded like a ward and might have been an insult.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The page showed the descending route beneath the desert. Seven narrowing turns surrounded the dark center. The line from Uruk still extended westward across the skin.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then the ink nearest the city began to fade.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: You never behave as though you know.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The drawn outline of Uruk paled.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The last mark to vanish was the western gate, though they had not passed through it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: In its place, a single vertical line darkened across the route.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It ran from the top of the page to the bottom.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Beside it, letters appeared in BAYL-ID-din's hand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The strokes formed slowly, pressing upward through the skin as if written from the other side.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Another word formed beneath the first.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek knew what it would say before the final mark appeared.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.note: Single word in Bel-iddin's hand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark in his palm went cold.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: en-HEH-doo checked her knives, then the dark cloth around her wrist, then the small pouch beneath her robe.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun looked down at her tablets.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek searched himself for an absence.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He remembered his mother sleeping in the repaired house. The archive. His father's face. KOO-rash raising the hammer. Uruk behind them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked from one face to another.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Names. Memories. Fingers. Whatever the stories say these gates take.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You would notice a missing finger.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I would prefer to establish that.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun pressed two fingers beneath her jaw as though checking for a pulse.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She watched him for a moment.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal knocked once between his hands.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: No answer came from beneath the ground.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The sun broke over the eastern horizon.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Light spread across the fields and reached Uruk's upper walls. The city stood behind them in brick, smoke, and gold.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek wrapped the journal and returned it to the satchel.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg finished loading the donkeys. Ninsun secured her tablets. en-HEH-doo climbed onto the brown animal before it could object and settled the reins in one hand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek mounted behind her pack frame. BAH-lahg took the gray donkey's lead rope and walked beside it, refusing to ride until he was satisfied the load had settled evenly.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun climbed onto the remaining space behind the waterskins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind them, Uruk disappeared one wall at a time as the land rose between the city and the desert.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ahead, the old road ran through dead fields toward the dunes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal rested silently against Zeek's ribs.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The first gate had taken its price.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: None of them knew what they had paid
